correctness.rationale: From the published survival \(\Pr(X\ge n)=\exp\{1-\mu^{n^\alpha}\}\), \(\mu^{n^\alpha}/n\to\infty\) for every \(\alpha>0\), \(\mu>1\). A mean-value-theorem estimate proves \(\mu^{(n+1)^\alpha}-\mu^{n^\alpha}\to\infty\), hence the adjacent-tail ratio tends to zero and the hazard tends to one. The same growth yields summability of \(e^{tn}\Pr(X=n)\) for every \(t>0\). The quantile formula follows by exact inversion of the CDF, and two elementary union/exponential bounds prove maximum concentration. The bundled checker evaluates only exact finite formulas and is not used to infer any infinite limit.

value.rationale: Heavy tails and long-tailed persistence are explicit headline motivations for the newly proposed DPham model. The finding gives a complete asymptotic tail classification over the entire admissible parameter space, not a single counterexample or finite plot. It proves finiteness of every positive exponential moment, identifies the terminal hazard, gives an exact/asymptotic upper-quantile formula, and quantifies sample maxima on a doubly-logarithmic scale. These results materially change how the model's extreme-count flexibility should be interpreted while leaving finite-sample fit claims untouched.
